# Standalone usage (primary)

## Loading a shape — `io/step_reader.py`

The entry point: turn a STEP file into the `TopoDS_Shape` every other function consumes.

| Function | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `load_shape(path, loader="auto")` | STEP → `TopoDS_Shape`. `loader` ∈ {`auto`, `build123d`, `cadquery`, `ocp`}; `auto` tries build123d → cadquery → OCP and takes the first success. Raises `OSError` if all fail. |
| `read_units()` | Configured STEP target unit (e.g. `"mm"`); falls back to `"mm"`. |
| `read_step_context(path)` | Parse the STEP HEADER → `dict(ap_schema, originating_system, preprocessor)` (AP203/214/242). |
| `heal_shape(shape, precision=None)` | Optional `ShapeFix_Shape` cleanup (tolerances, tiny edges). May change topology. |

```python
from step_2_aag.io.step_reader import load_shape
shape = load_shape("part.step")
```

## Core geometry & properties

**`core/geom.py`** — small pure helpers:
`xyz(p)` (point→`[x,y,z]`), `unit(v)`, `dot(a,b)`, `is_reversed(shape)`,
`outward_normal(face, point)` (orientation-corrected `gp_Vec`),
`edge_midpoint_and_tangent(edge)` → `(gp_Pnt, gp_Vec)`,
`edge_orientation_in_face(edge, face)` (co-edge orientation).

**`core/enums.py`** — lookup tables: `SURFACE_TYPE_NAMES`, `CURVE_TYPE_NAMES`, `CONTINUITY_NAMES`,
and the type classes `FREEFORM_TYPES`, `DEVELOPABLE_TYPES`.

**`core/traversal.py`** — `map_shapes(shape, subtype)`, `count(shape, subtype)`,
`list_solids(shape)`, `face_solid_index(shape, face_map, solids)`.

**`core/mass_properties.py`** (all take a shape/sub-shape):

| Function | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `compute_volume(shape)` / `compute_surface_area(shape)` | volume / total area |
| `compute_face_area(face)` / `compute_edge_length(edge)` | single face area / edge arc length |
| `compute_centroid(shape)` | `[x, y, z]` volume centroid |
| `compute_inertia(shape)` | `{principal_moments, has_symmetry_axis, has_symmetry_point}` |
| `principal_axes(shape)` | `(centroid_pnt, [a1, a2, a3])` principal inertia axes |
| `compute_mass_properties(shape)` | aggregate: volume, area, A/V ratio, centroid, inertia |

**`core/bounding_box.py`** — `compute_aabb(shape)` → `{min, max, diagonal}`;
`compute_inertia_aligned_box(shape)` → oriented box `{half_sizes, extents, volume, axes, origin}`.

## Surface features — `features/surfaces.py`

| Function | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `surface_info(face, adaptor=None)` | type + freeform/developable flags + `analytic` params + gauss-map + outward normal |
| `surface_metrics_of(face, adaptor=None)` | area, perimeter, centroid, bbox, UV bounds, closed/periodic flags, wire/loop counts |
| `surface_curvature_of(face, adaptor=None)` | principal curvatures (min/max/mean/gaussian) at the UV midpoint |
| `surface_type_name(adaptor)` | `plane`/`cylinder`/…/`bspline` |
| `analytic_parameters(adaptor, stype, uv)` | per-type params (radius, axis, half-angle, span, B-spline structure, …) |
| `gauss_map(stype, analytic)` | spherical normal-image descriptor (point / arc / band / …) |
| `principal_curvatures(adaptor, u, v)` | curvatures + normal at a UV point |
| `outer_wire_perimeter(face)` | perimeter of the outer wire |

`face` is any `TopoDS_Face`; an adaptor is built internally if not supplied.

## Edge features & adjacency — `features/edges.py`

| Function | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `build_adjacency(ctx)` | `(links, stats)` — face-pair links (MultiGraph, keyed) + open/nonmanifold/seam counts. Needs a `GeometryContext` (cheap; not a graph). |
| `edge_geometry_of(edge)` | curve type, length, tolerance, closed/degenerated, curvature, per-type geometry, endpoints |
| `edge_convexity_of(edge, fa, fb)` | continuity + convex/concave/tangential + normal/dihedral angle |
| `edge_coedges_of(edge, fa, fb)` | co-edge orientation (`forward`/`reversed`) per adjacent face |
| `continuity_name(edge, fa, fb)` | geometric continuity `C0/G1/…` |
| `classify_convexity(edge, fa, fb, continuity)` | convexity + angles |

`fa`/`fb` are the two adjacent faces (from `GeometryContext(shape).edge_faces` or a link's
`_fa`/`_fb`).

## Grouping & whole-shape features

| Function | Module | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `group_coaxial(records, angular_tolerance, model_tolerance)` | coaxial | coaxial cylinder/cone/torus groups + dominant rotation axis |
| `group_orientations(records, angular_tolerance)` | orientation | faces grouped by outward normal + distinct-orientation count |
| `mirror_symmetry(shape, model_tolerance, diagonal=None, n_faces=None)` | symmetry | per-principal-plane mirror distance + symmetry verdict |
| `min_wall_thickness(planar_faces, angular_tolerance, model_tolerance)` | thickness | smallest gap between antiparallel planar faces + the pair |
| `topology_summary(shape, counts, adjacency_stats)` | topology | validity, watertight/manifold, Euler characteristic, genus |
| `compute_distributions(node_records, links)` | topology | type/convexity/continuity histograms + area/edge-length balances |

`records` are per-face dicts (e.g. from `surface_info`); `planar_faces` is a list of
`(face_id, TopoDS_Face, outward_normal)`. `volume.py` adds nothing new standalone — call
`compute_mass_properties` / `compute_aabb` / `compute_inertia_aligned_box` from `core` directly.

## Example

```python
from step_2_aag.io.step_reader import load_shape
from step_2_aag.occ import TopAbs_FACE, topods
from step_2_aag.core.traversal import map_shapes
from step_2_aag.core.mass_properties import compute_mass_properties
from step_2_aag.features.surfaces import surface_info
from step_2_aag.features.coaxial import group_coaxial

shape = load_shape("part.step")
mass  = compute_mass_properties(shape)                     # volume / area / centroid / inertia

faces = map_shapes(shape, TopAbs_FACE)
info  = surface_info(topods.Face(faces.FindKey(1)))        # one face, no context

records = [surface_info(topods.Face(faces.FindKey(i))) for i in range(1, faces.Size() + 1)]
coax    = group_coaxial(records, angular_tolerance=1e-4, model_tolerance=1e-6)
```

---

# The AAG graph

`GeometryContext(shape)` (`core/context.py`) gives cached, shared access to one shape: face/edge
maps, `edge_faces` adjacency, cached surface adaptors, and derived `model_tolerance` /
`angular_tolerance`. It underpins the builder and the adjacency-based functions.

Features register themselves via the `core/registry.py` decorators (`@face_feature`,
`@edge_feature`, `@graph_feature`); importing `features/` runs them in a fixed order (`surfaces`
first, since later features read the node records it fills).

## `graph/builder.py`

`build_graph(shape, features=None, *, source_file=None, units=None, context=None,
capture_provenance=False)` → **one `networkx.MultiGraph` per file** (node ID = 0-based global
face index; `solid_index` per node). Requires `networkx`.

**You choose which features to compute** — the right set depends heavily on the part's geometry,
so there is no "run everything" default:

- `features=None` (nothing chosen) → **no graph is built**; returns a description string of all
  available features (from `describe_features()`), so you can pick deliberately.
- `features=[]` → the bare skeleton (nodes + edges, no feature attributes).
- `features=[...]` → exactly those features. Unknown names or missing dependencies raise a
  `ValueError` explaining what to add.

Introspect the catalogue with `feature_catalog()` (`{level: {name: summary}}`) or
`describe_features()` (formatted text). Selectable features:

- **Nodes (faces):** `surface_type`, `surface_metrics`, `surface_curvature`, `face_edge_stats`, `inner_loops`.
- **Edges:** `edge_geometry`, `edge_convexity`, `edge_coedges`.
- **Graph:** `mass_properties`, `bounding_boxes`, `topology_stats`, `distributions`, `symmetry`, `wall_thickness`, `coaxial`, `orientation_groups`.

Some features read fields others produce, so they must be selected together (the builder
enforces this):

| Feature | Requires |
| --- | --- |
| `coaxial`, `wall_thickness` | `surface_type` |
| `orientation_groups` | `surface_type`, `surface_metrics` |
| `distributions` | `surface_type`, `surface_metrics`, `edge_geometry`, `edge_convexity` |
| `face_edge_stats`, `inner_loops` | `edge_convexity` |

`capture_provenance=True` attaches `G.field_provenance` (which extractor first produced each
field). `face_edge_stats` and `inner_loops` read builder-populated context state, so they only
run inside a graph build — every other feature is also available standalone above.

```python
from step_2_aag.graph.builder import build_graph, describe_features

print(describe_features())                       # discover what's available
G = build_graph(shape, features=[                # then compute only what you need
    "surface_type", "surface_metrics", "coaxial",
])
```

## `io/exporter.py`

| Function | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `graph_to_node_link(graph)` | Graph → JSON-serializable dict (`nx.node_link_data`) |
| `graph_to_json(graph, indent=2, round_floats=None)` | Graph → JSON string |
| `save_graph_json(graph, path, indent=2, round_floats=None)` | Write JSON to `path` (UTF-8); returns the path |

```python
from step_2_aag.graph.builder import build_graph
from step_2_aag.io.exporter import save_graph_json

G = build_graph(load_shape("part.step"), features=["surface_type", "coaxial"],
                source_file="part.step")
save_graph_json(G, "part.json", round_floats=6)
```

"""Deterministic geometry extraction for bracket-373 (and reference parts).

Usage: python geometry.py <step_path> [out_json]
Writes a JSON dict of key figures; reads only the given STEP file.
"""
import json
import math
import sys

from step_2_aag.io.step_reader import load_shape
from step_2_aag.occ import TopAbs_FACE, TopAbs_EDGE, topods
from step_2_aag.core.traversal import map_shapes, count, list_solids
from step_2_aag.core.mass_properties import compute_mass_properties
from step_2_aag.core.bounding_box import compute_aabb
from step_2_aag.features.surfaces import surface_info
from step_2_aag.features.coaxial import group_coaxial


def _vec3(v):
    return [round(v.X(), 6), round(v.Y(), 6), round(v.Z(), 6)]


def extract(step_path: str) -> dict:
    shape = load_shape(step_path)

    mass = compute_mass_properties(shape)
    aabb = compute_aabb(shape)
    n_faces = count(shape, TopAbs_FACE)
    n_edges = count(shape, TopAbs_EDGE)
    solids = list_solids(shape)

    face_map = map_shapes(shape, TopAbs_FACE)
    records = [surface_info(topods.Face(face_map.FindKey(i))) for i in range(1, face_map.Size() + 1)]

    type_hist = {}
    cyl_records = []
    for r in records:
        t = r.get("type", "unknown")
        type_hist[t] = type_hist.get(t, 0) + 1
        if t == "cylinder":
            a = r.get("analytic", {}) or {}
            cyl_records.append({
                "face_id": r.get("id"),
                "radius": round(a.get("radius", float("nan")), 6),
                "axis": _vec3(a["axis_direction"]) if a.get("axis_direction") is not None else None,
                "center": _vec3(a["center"]) if a.get("center") is not None else None,
                "area_mm2": round(r.get("area", 0.0), 4),
            })

    # coaxial groups (holes / rounded ends)
    try:
        coax = group_coaxial(records, angular_tolerance=1e-3, model_tolerance=1e-5)
        coax_summary = []
        for g in coax.get("groups", []):
            coax_summary.append({
                "axis": _vec3(g["axis_direction"]) if g.get("axis_direction") is not None else None,
                "radii": [round(x, 4) for x in g.get("radii", [])],
                "n_faces": len(g.get("face_ids", [])),
            })
    except Exception as e:  # pragma: no cover
        coax_summary = f"error: {e}"

    # inner loops => through holes (cylindrical faces with a hole through the part)
    def _axis_key(a):
        if not a:
            return None
        u = [abs(x) for x in a]
        m = max(u)
        return [round(u[i] / m, 4) for i in range(3)]

    holes = []
    for c in cyl_records:
        # a through-hole face spans the full wall thickness; capture axis + radius
        holes.append({"radius_mm": c["radius"], "axis_dir": c["axis"], "area_mm2": c["area_mm2"]})

    bbox_dims = [round(aabb["max"][i] - aabb["min"][i], 4) for i in range(3)]

    return {
        "file": step_path,
        "solids": len(solids),
        "n_faces": n_faces,
        "n_edges": n_edges,
        "face_type_histogram": type_hist,
        "volume_mm3": round(mass["volume"], 4),
        "surface_area_mm2": round(mass["area"], 4),
        "centroid_mm": mass.get("centroid"),
        "aabb_min_mm": [round(x, 4) for x in aabb["min"]],
        "aabb_max_mm": [round(x, 4) for x in aabb["max"]],
        "bbox_dims_mm": bbox_dims,
        "bbox_volume_mm3": round(bbox_dims[0] * bbox_dims[1] * bbox_dims[2], 4),
        "volume_to_bbox_ratio": round(mass["volume"] / (bbox_dims[0] * bbox_dims[1] * bbox_dims[2]), 4),
        "cylindrical_faces": cyl_records,
        "coaxial_groups": coax_summary,
        "cylinder_axes_normalized": sorted({_axis_key(c["axis"]) for c in cyl_records if c["axis"]}),
    }


def main():
    step_path = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "/workspace/file/bracket-373.step"
    out_json = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None
    data = extract(step_path)
    text = json.dumps(data, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)

"""Unit price calculation - bracket-373 (steel L-bracket, 7.92 x 6.35 x 11.51 mm).

Follows the company's calculation pattern (see EXAMPLE_*.md and FINDINGS.md > Transfer):
  * material = FULL raw-stock volume x density x EUR/kg x 1.2 surcharge
  * every process line = minutes/60 x hourly rate x 1.2 margin
  * fixed-per-batch lines are divided by the quantity (degression)
  * no separate tolerance/surface-finish/tooling lines; "other costs" = 0
  * each of the three blocks is rounded to cents before summing

All minutes come from FINDINGS.md > Transfer (booked time at the requested batch size,
basis noted per line). Complexity = 3/10, workholding setups = 1 (3-axis) -> we sit at
the company's floor booking for a simple small part, with machining one step above the
797/1016 floor because of thinner walls (1.19 mm), an H7 bore and a larger stock block.
"""

import json
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

QUANTITIES = (1, 10, 50)

# --- Input data ---------------------------------------------------------
# From the request (INPUT.md): flat steel stock 14 x 10 x 13 mm, 7.90 g/cm3.
STOCK_MM = (14.0, 10.0, 13.0)
DENSITY_G_CM3 = 7.90
STEEL_PRICE_EUR_KG = 6.00   # assumption D6: steel net price, bracketed by reference alu levels

# Hourly rates from the request (known manufacturing processes).
RATE = {
    "work_preparation": 60.0,
    "machine_operator": 60.0,
    "saw": 20.0,
    "milling_machine": 75.0,
    "deburring": 65.0,
    "checking_qa": 70.0,
    "packing": 40.0,
}

MARGIN = 1.2                # 20 % margin on every line (company pattern)


def _line(minutes, rate_key, quantity, fixed_per_batch):
    """minutes/60 x rate x 1.2; fixed lines are spread over the batch."""
    value = minutes / 60 * RATE[rate_key] * MARGIN
    return value / quantity if fixed_per_batch else value


def costs(quantity):
    """The three cost blocks per piece for a batch of `quantity` pieces."""
    # --- Material ----------------------------------------------------
    # Full stock volume (incl. offcut/chips ~93 %), company pattern.
    volume_cm3 = STOCK_MM[0] * STOCK_MM[1] * STOCK_MM[2] / 1000      # 18.2 cm3
    weight_kg = volume_cm3 * DENSITY_G_CM3 / 1000                    # 0.1438 kg
    material = weight_kg * STEEL_PRICE_EUR_KG * MARGIN               # -> ~1.03 EUR

    # --- Processes ---------------------------------------------------
    # One clamping on a vertical mill (3-axis); saw blank first.
    process = 0.0

    # Work preparation - labour (fixed per batch)
    # 30 min: company floor for a simple small part (797/1016), CAM + routing.
    process += _line(30, "work_preparation", quantity, True)

    # Machine operator - labour
    # 30 min setup fixed per batch: company floor; thin-wall clamping (soft jaws).
    process += _line(30, "machine_operator", quantity, True)
    # 1 min/pc saw handling: small references (1025 uses 2 for a 457 cm3 stock).
    process += _line(1, "machine_operator", quantity, False)
    # 2 min/pc mill load/unload: small references.
    process += _line(2, "machine_operator", quantity, False)

    # Saw, without employee - machine
    # 2 min/pc: two cuts to release the 14x10x13 blank from flat stock (797/1016 level).
    process += _line(2, "saw", quantity, False)

    # Milling machine - without employee - machine
    # 30 min setup fixed per batch: company floor (all small references).
    process += _line(30, "milling_machine", quantity, True)
    # 5 min/pc machining incl. drilling: L-notch ~5.9x6.35 mm up to 10.3 mm deep with
    # 1.19 mm walls, both side faces, R3 end rounds + 0.35 flat tip, drill O3.5 (horizontal)
    # and O2.16 H7 (vertical). Above 797's 4 min (shallow slots, no H7 bore), below
    # 224's 7 min (bigger part, 3 holes + slot).
    process += _line(5, "milling_machine", quantity, False)

    # Deburring - labour
    # 3 min/pc: company floor for small parts; 2 hole burrs + thin-wall edges (ISO 13715).
    process += _line(3, "deburring", quantity, False)

    # Checking QA - labour
    # 10 min first article fixed per batch: full drawing check incl. O2.16 H7 gauge pin
    # and 11.51 +/-0.05 height (same as all references except the big one).
    process += _line(10, "checking_qa", quantity, True)
    # 1 min/pc in-line check: height + both bores (all references except the big one).
    process += _line(1, "checking_qa", quantity, False)

    # Packing - labour
    # 5 min per batch (all references) + 0.5 min/pc (small references, tiny part).
    process += _line(5, "packing", quantity, True)
    process += _line(0.5, "packing", quantity, False)

    # --- Other costs -------------------------------------------------
    other = 0.0   # no flat batch costs in any reference calculation

    return material, process, other


def _cents(value):
    """Round to cents, halves away from zero."""
    return Decimal(value).quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def unit_price(quantity):
    """Price per piece in EUR for a batch of `quantity` pieces.

    Every block is rounded to cents on its own before the three are added up
    (company pattern - rounding only the total would be a cent off).
    """
    return float(sum(_cents(block) for block in costs(quantity)))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # sanity: also show the reference envelope from findings.json
    try:
        with open("/workspace/findings.json") as f:
            _f = json.load(f)
        print("part volume_mm3:", _f["volume_mm3"], "| bbox_mm:", _f["bbox_dims_mm"])
        print("reference unit prices (EUR):")
        for _eid, _r in _f.get("reference_examples", {}).items():
            print("  ", _eid, _r["unit_price_eur"])
    except FileNotFoundError:
        pass

    _head = ("quantity", "material", "processes", "other", "EUR/piece")
    print("{:>10} {:>10} {:>10} {:>10} {:>12}".format(*_head))
    for _q in QUANTITIES:
        _m, _p, _o = costs(_q)
        print(f"{_q:>10} {_m:>10.2f} {_p:>10.2f} {_o:>10.2f} {unit_price(_q):>12.2f}")

    import merge_refs  # re-merges refs into the fresh findings.json
    merge_refs.main() if hasattr(merge_refs, "main") else None
    print("[2/3] reference examples merged into findings.json")


def run_costing():
    import costing
    print("[3/3] unit prices (net EUR/piece):")
    estimates = {}
    for q in costing.QUANTITIES:

              f"{'inside/band-consistent' if ok else 'DEVIATION - see FINDINGS.md Transfer'}")


if __name__ == "__main__":

Visual Survey (renders: view_iso/front/top/right/bottom.png)

Part class: small milled L-bracket (thin-walled, prismatic + 2 bores + 2 rounds). Very small: bbox 7.92 × 6.35 × 11.51 mm, volume ≈ 118 mm³ (~0.93 g steel).

Features (confirmed by renders + geometry code): - Vertical plate leg: 6.35 wide × ~10.3 tall, thickness 1.19 mm, one Ø3.5 through-hole (axis horizontal, through the thin direction), hole center 6.8 mm above the bottom face. - Foot/base leg: D-shaped plan profile (length 7.92 incl. plate thickness, width 6.35), thickness 1.19 mm, rounded end made of two R3 quarter-arcs + a 0.35 mm flat at the tip, one Ø2.16 through-hole (axis vertical) centered ~4.8 mm from the plate back face (≈ center of the rounding). - Holes: 2 through-holes total (1 horizontal Ø3.5, 1 vertical Ø2.16). No blind holes, no threads, no freeform surfaces. - Chamfers/fillets: none visible in model except the R3 end rounds; drawing references ISO 13715 for edges → light edge break/deburr expected. - Access: all features open to atmosphere; no undercuts; all machinable on a 3-axis mill. 5-axis NOT required.

Workholding setups estimate: - 3-axis: 1–2 setups (see Manufacturing Assessment). - 5-axis: not needed.

Drawing Analysis (bracket-373.pdf, 1 page, SOLIDWORKS title block)

Read with high confidence (full page + zoomed crops): - Dimensions: overall height 11.51 ±0.05 mm (only explicitly tolerated dimension); plate width 6.35; foot length 7.92; hole centers 6.8 (plate hole) and 4.8 (foot hole); leg thickness 1.19; rounding R3. - Hole callouts: plate hole Ø3.5 (no individual tolerance → general tolerance applies); foot hole Ø2.16 +0.02/0.00 (H7-like fit, the tightest feature on the part). - General tolerances: ISO 2768-mK (medium grade; e.g. ±0.1 mm for 3–6 mm dims, ±0.2 for 10–14… per m class). - Principles: ISO 8015; dimension tolerance ISO 14405-1; angular ISO 14405-3. - Surface finish: only "Oberfläche: ISO 21920" (the symbol standard) — no Ra values specified anywhere → normal machining finish acceptable. - Edges (Kanten): ISO 13715 → edge break / burr removal required (deburring line justified). - Material per drawing: X8CrNiS18-9 (1.4305) — austenitic stainless steel. Request's structured data says "steel, 7.90 g/cm³" (which is exactly the density of 1.4305) → consistent; I price as steel-grade flat stock per the request and note the drawing grade. - No GD&T (no datums, no runout/position), no heat treatment, no coating, no inspection callouts beyond the above. - Title block: "SOLIDWORKS Lehrprodukt – Nur für Lehrzwecke" (teaching part), created 16.11.26 by [Name entfernt]. Scale 5:1.

Tolerance level summary: medium (ISO 2768-mK) with one fine bore Ø2.16 H7 and one ±0.05 overall height → ordinary precision drilling + careful setup; no grinding/lapping needed.

Manufacturing Assessment (Phase 4)

Machine choice: vertical milling center (3-axis sufficient; company examples run this family on a "5-axis milling machine, one clamping" — no 5th-axis motion needed for our part). One clamping setup.

Raw stock (given): flat 14×10×13 mm steel block = 1.82 cm³ = 14.4 g at 7.90 g/cm³. Part is 117.8 mm³ (0.118 cm³) → ~93 % of the stock becomes chips (more than any reference, which ran 69–89 %). Material charged on FULL stock volume per company pattern.

Process chain (one setup): 1. Saw/cut blank from flat stock (saw line, ~2 min/pc like the small references — "2 cuts from plate"). 2. 3-axis milling, 1 clamping: face the bottom (datum), mill the L-notch between the legs (~5.9×6.35 mm, up to ~10.3 mm deep), both side faces to 6.35 width, R3 end rounds + 0.35 flat tip, then drill Ø3.5 (horizontal, through 1.19 mm plate) and Ø2.16 H7 (vertical, through 1.19 mm foot). Drilling is booked INSIDE the machining minutes (no example uses the separate 65 €/h drilling rate). 3. Deburring (ISO 13715 edge break + hole burrs) — thin walls make burrs prominent; ~3 min/pc. 4. QA: first article per batch (incl. Ø2.16 H7 bore check with pin/gauge, 11.51 ±0.05 overall) + in-line check per piece. 5. Packing per batch + per piece.

Workholding risk: legs are only 1.19 mm thick → clamp on the wide faces (foot bottom + plate back), light pressure, expect soft jaws; chatter is the main quality risk on the deep L-notch with a small end mill. No undercuts, no thin-web flip needed: one setup machines everything reachable from the top/front; the two hole axes (X and Z) are both accessible in one clamping.

Tolerance handling: ISO 2768-mK + 11.51 ±0.05 + Ø2.16 +0.02/0. No example charges a tolerance/finish surcharge — effort is absorbed into machining, deburring and QA minutes. Follow that (see Transfer).

Inspection strategy: first article = full drawing check (height 11.51 ±0.05, hole Ø3.5 general, bore Ø2.16 H7 with gauge pin, R3 profile, thickness 1.19); in-line = height + both bores per piece.

Complexity rating: 3 / 10. (Anchor 3–5 = several setups/several feature types/moderate tolerances; we are at the LOW end of that band: only ONE setup, few features, but thin 1.19 mm walls + one H7 bore keep it above 2.)

Deburring per pc 3 company floor for small parts; 2 hole burrs + thin-wall edges (ISO 13715) high
QA per piece per pc 1 all refs except big one high
Packing per piece per pc 0.5 small refs (tiny part) high

Material: stock 14×10×13 mm = 1.82 cm³ × 7.90 g/cm³ = 14.4 g; price assumption 6.00 €/kg net (steel per request; drawing names 1.4305 stainless — between carbon-steel ~3.5 and 1.4305 ~8.5 €/kg; sensitivity is <±0.05 €/pc) × 1.2 surcharge = 0.10 €/pc.

Price band per requested quantity (from the reference envelope: my part sits between the 797/1016 floor and the 224/567 mid tier): - qty 1: 140–175 € (confidence high — inside the 150–177 € envelope of the four smaller refs) - qty 10: 28–40 € (refs 29–42 €) - qty 50: 18–30 € (refs 18–30 €)

Deviations vs references: ABOVE the 797/1016 floor because of thinner walls (more careful machining), an H7 bore and a deeper L-notch; material per piece (0.10 €) is in the same small range as 797's 0.23 € because our stock is much smaller by volume (1.82 vs 11.88 cm³) though steel is denser and dearer per kg. BELOW 224/567 because the part is ~8–180× smaller with fewer features. No tolerance/finish surcharge (pattern-consistent).

Decisions & Confidence

  • D1: Part is milled from the given flat stock 14×10×13 mm (request data), not bent sheet — the request fixes raw stock form/dimensions and the process list (saw + mill + drill) supports a cut-then-machine flow. (confidence: high for using the given stock; strategy to be calibrated vs. examples)
  • D2: No 5-axis, no turning, no threads, no coating — scope is saw/cut → 3-axis milling → drilling → deburr → QA → pack. (confidence: high)
  • D3: Material priced per request "steel @7.90 g/cm³"; drawing says 1.4305 — density identical; price difference small and noted in costing assumptions. (confidence: medium)
  • D4: Complexity kept at 3/10 after reference review (no change): one setup, few features, thin walls + H7 bore = low end of the 3–5 band. (confidence: high)
  • D5: No tolerance/surface-finish surcharge lines — all five references absorb that effort into machining/deburring/QA minutes; following the company pattern exactly. (confidence: high)
  • D6: Steel net price 6.00 €/kg assumed (no steel example exists; bracketed between the alu 6.09–8.10 €/kg levels and carbon-steel market levels). Impact on unit price < ±0.20 €. (confidence: medium)

Run: python main.py

import json

"""Deterministic geometry extraction for bracket-373 (and reference parts).

Usage: python geometry.py <step_path> [out_json]
Writes a JSON dict of key figures; reads only the given STEP file.
"""
import json
import sys

from step_2_aag.io.step_reader import load_shape
from step_2_aag.occ import TopAbs_FACE, TopAbs_EDGE, topods
from step_2_aag.core.traversal import map_shapes, count, list_solids
from step_2_aag.core.mass_properties import compute_mass_properties
from step_2_aag.core.bounding_box import compute_aabb
from step_2_aag.features.surfaces import surface_info
from step_2_aag.features.coaxial import group_coaxial


def _vec3(v):
    return [round(v.X(), 6), round(v.Y(), 6), round(v.Z(), 6)]


def extract(step_path: str) -> dict:
    shape = load_shape(step_path)

    mass = compute_mass_properties(shape)
    aabb = compute_aabb(shape)
    n_faces = count(shape, TopAbs_FACE)
    n_edges = count(shape, TopAbs_EDGE)
    solids = list_solids(shape)

    face_map = map_shapes(shape, TopAbs_FACE)
    records = [surface_info(topods.Face(face_map.FindKey(i))) for i in range(1, face_map.Size() + 1)]

    def _tname(t):
        return str(t).strip("'\"")

    type_hist = {}
    cyl_records = []
    for r in records:
        t = _tname(r.get("surface_type", "unknown"))
        type_hist[t] = type_hist.get(t, 0) + 1
        if t == "cylinder":
            a = r.get("analytic", {}) or {}
            cyl_records.append({
                "face_id": r.get("id"),
                "radius": round(a.get("radius", float("nan")), 6),
                "diameter_mm": round(2 * a.get("radius", float("nan")), 4),
                "axis": [round(x, 6) for x in a["axis_direction"]] if a.get("axis_direction") is not None else None,
                "axis_location": [round(x, 6) for x in a["axis_location"]] if a.get("axis_location") is not None else None,
                "angular_span_rad": round(a.get("angular_span_rad", float("nan")), 4),
                "is_full_revolution": a.get("is_full_revolution"),
                "axial_length_mm": round(a.get("axial_length", float("nan")), 4),
            })

    # coaxial groups (holes / rounded ends)
    try:
        coax = group_coaxial(records, angular_tolerance=1e-3, model_tolerance=1e-5)
        coax_summary = []
        for g in coax.get("groups", []):
            coax_summary.append({
                "axis": _vec3(g["axis_direction"]) if g.get("axis_direction") is not None else None,
                "radii": [round(x, 4) for x in g.get("radii", [])],
                "n_faces": len(g.get("face_ids", [])),
            })
    except Exception as e:  # pragma: no cover
        coax_summary = f"error: {e}"

    def _axis_key(a):
        if not a:
            return None
        u = [abs(x) for x in a]
        m = max(u)
        return [round(u[i] / m, 4) for i in range(3)]

    # full-revolution cylinders = bores/holes; partial spans = rounds/fillets
    through_holes = [c for c in cyl_records if c.get("is_full_revolution")]
    rounds = [c for c in cyl_records if not c.get("is_full_revolution")]

    bbox_dims = [round(aabb["max"][i] - aabb["min"][i], 4) for i in range(3)]

    return {
        "file": step_path,
        "solids": len(solids),
        "n_faces": n_faces,
        "n_edges": n_edges,
        "face_type_histogram": type_hist,
        "volume_mm3": round(mass["volume"], 4),
        "surface_area_mm2": round(mass["surface_area"], 4),
        "centroid_mm": mass.get("center_of_mass"),
        "aabb_min_mm": [round(x, 4) for x in aabb["min"]],
        "aabb_max_mm": [round(x, 4) for x in aabb["max"]],
        "bbox_dims_mm": bbox_dims,
        "bbox_volume_mm3": round(bbox_dims[0] * bbox_dims[1] * bbox_dims[2], 4),
        "volume_to_bbox_ratio": round(mass["volume"] / (bbox_dims[0] * bbox_dims[1] * bbox_dims[2]), 4),
        "cylindrical_faces": cyl_records,
        "through_holes": through_holes,
        "rounds_fillet_arcs": rounds,
        "n_through_holes": len(through_holes),
        "n_rounds": len(rounds),
        "coaxial_groups": coax_summary,
        "cylinder_axes_normalized": [list(t) for t in sorted({tuple(_axis_key(c["axis"])) for c in cyl_records if c["axis"]})],
    }


def main():
    step_path = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "/workspace/file/bracket-373.step"
    out_json = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None
    data = extract(step_path)
    text = json.dumps(data, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
    if out_json:
        with open(out_json, "w") as f:
            f.write(text)
        print(f"wrote {out_json}")
    else:
        print(text)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Unit price calculation - bracket-373 (steel L-bracket, 7.92 x 6.35 x 11.51 mm).

Follows the company's calculation pattern (see EXAMPLE_*.md and FINDINGS.md > Transfer):
  * material = FULL raw-stock volume x density x EUR/kg x 1.2 surcharge
  * every process line = minutes/60 x hourly rate x 1.2 margin
  * fixed-per-batch lines are divided by the quantity (degression)
  * no separate tolerance/surface-finish/tooling lines; "other costs" = 0
  * each of the three blocks is rounded to cents before summing

All minutes come from FINDINGS.md > Transfer (booked time at the requested batch size,
basis noted per line). Complexity = 3/10, workholding setups = 1 (3-axis) -> we sit at
the company's floor booking for a simple small part, with machining one step above the
797/1016 floor because of thinner walls (1.19 mm), an H7 bore and a deeper L-notch.
"""

import json
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

QUANTITIES = (1, 10, 50)

# --- Input data ---------------------------------------------------------
# From the request (INPUT.md): flat steel stock 14 x 10 x 13 mm, 7.90 g/cm3.
STOCK_MM = (14.0, 10.0, 13.0)
DENSITY_G_CM3 = 7.90
STEEL_PRICE_EUR_KG = 6.00   # assumption D6: steel net price, bracketed by reference alu levels

# Hourly rates from the request (known manufacturing processes).
RATE = {
    "work_preparation": 60.0,
    "machine_operator": 60.0,
    "saw": 20.0,
    "milling_machine": 75.0,
    "deburring": 65.0,
    "checking_qa": 70.0,
    "packing": 40.0,
}

MARGIN = 1.2                # 20 % margin on every line (company pattern)


def _line(minutes, rate_key, quantity, fixed_per_batch):
    """minutes/60 x rate x 1.2; fixed lines are spread over the batch."""
    value = minutes / 60 * RATE[rate_key] * MARGIN
    return value / quantity if fixed_per_batch else value


def costs(quantity):
    """The three cost blocks per piece for a batch of `quantity` pieces."""
    # --- Material ----------------------------------------------------
    # Full stock volume (incl. offcut/chips ~93 %), company pattern.
    volume_cm3 = STOCK_MM[0] * STOCK_MM[1] * STOCK_MM[2] / 1000      # 1.82 cm3
    weight_kg = volume_cm3 * DENSITY_G_CM3 / 1000                    # 0.01438 kg
    material = weight_kg * STEEL_PRICE_EUR_KG * MARGIN               # -> ~0.10 EUR

    # --- Processes ---------------------------------------------------
    # One clamping on a vertical mill (3-axis); saw blank first.
    process = 0.0

    # Work preparation - labour (fixed per batch)
    # 30 min: company floor for a simple small part (797/1016), CAM + routing.
    process += _line(30, "work_preparation", quantity, True)

    # Machine operator - labour
    # 30 min setup fixed per batch: company floor; thin-wall clamping (soft jaws).
    process += _line(30, "machine_operator", quantity, True)
    # 1 min/pc saw handling: small references (1025 uses 2 for a 457 cm3 stock).
    process += _line(1, "machine_operator", quantity, False)
    # 2 min/pc mill load/unload: small references.
    process += _line(2, "machine_operator", quantity, False)

    # Saw, without employee - machine
    # 2 min/pc: two cuts to release the 14x10x13 blank from flat stock (797/1016 level).
    process += _line(2, "saw", quantity, False)

    # Milling machine - without employee - machine
    # 30 min setup fixed per batch: company floor (all small references).
    process += _line(30, "milling_machine", quantity, True)
    # 5 min/pc machining incl. drilling: L-notch ~5.9x6.35 mm up to 10.3 mm deep with
    # 1.19 mm walls, both side faces, R3 end rounds + 0.35 flat tip, drill O3.5 (horizontal)
    # and O2.16 H7 (vertical). Above 797's 4 min (shallow slots, no H7 bore), below
    # 224's 7 min (bigger part, 3 holes + slot).
    process += _line(5, "milling_machine", quantity, False)

    # Deburring - labour
    # 3 min/pc: company floor for small parts; 2 hole burrs + thin-wall edges (ISO 13715).
    process += _line(3, "deburring", quantity, False)

    # Checking QA - labour
    # 10 min first article fixed per batch: full drawing check incl. O2.16 H7 gauge pin
    # and 11.51 +/-0.05 height (same as all references except the big one).
    process += _line(10, "checking_qa", quantity, True)
    # 1 min/pc in-line check: height + both bores (all references except the big one).
    process += _line(1, "checking_qa", quantity, False)

    # Packing - labour
    # 5 min per batch (all references) + 0.5 min/pc (small references, tiny part).
    process += _line(5, "packing", quantity, True)
    process += _line(0.5, "packing", quantity, False)

    # --- Other costs -------------------------------------------------
    other = 0.0   # no flat batch costs in any reference calculation

    return material, process, other


def _cents(value):
    """Round to cents, halves away from zero."""
    return Decimal(value).quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def unit_price(quantity):
    """Price per piece in EUR for a batch of `quantity` pieces.

    Every block is rounded to cents on its own before the three are added up
    (company pattern - rounding only the total would be a cent off).
    """
    return float(sum(_cents(block) for block in costs(quantity)))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # sanity: also show the reference envelope from findings.json
    try:
        with open("/workspace/findings.json") as f:
            _f = json.load(f)
        print("part volume_mm3:", _f["volume_mm3"], "| bbox_mm:", _f["bbox_dims_mm"])
        print("reference unit prices (EUR):")
        for _eid, _r in _f.get("reference_examples", {}).items():
            print("  ", _eid, _r["unit_price_eur"])
    except FileNotFoundError:
        pass

    _head = ("quantity", "material", "processes", "other", "EUR/piece")
    print("{:>10} {:>10} {:>10} {:>10} {:>12}".format(*_head))
    for _q in QUANTITIES:
        _m, _p, _o = costs(_q)
        print(f"{_q:>10} {_m:>10.2f} {_p:>10.2f} {_o:>10.2f} {unit_price(_q):>12.2f}")

from step_2_aag.core.traversal import map_shapes

    m = surface_metrics_of(face)
